diagnostic_evidence.quote: $a(t)\in C([0,T])$ is a real-valued function, and $|a'(t)|<c, t\in [0,T]$.
The time signals excited at different moments can be separated under the Assumption \ref{sump}.

issues.failure_explanation: The time support of the j-th pulse in the far field at direction $\hat x$ is $[t_j-\sup(\hat x\cdot D_j)/c,\ t_j-\inf(\hat x\cdot D_j)/c]$. Non-overlap with pulse $j-1$ requires $c(t_j-t_{j-1})>\sup(\hat x\cdot D_j)-\inf(\hat x\cdot D_{j-1})$. With $D_j=D_{j-1}+\Delta$, $\Delta=a(t_j)-a(t_{j-1})$, the right side equals the width of $D_{j-1}$ plus $\hat x\cdot\Delta$, which can be as large as $\mathrm{diam}\,D_{j-1}+|\Delta|$ with $|\Delta|$ up to (almost) $c(t_j-t_{j-1})$. E.g. a ball of radius $r$, $c=1$, moving toward the observer at speed $v$ close to 1 with $t_j-t_{j-1}=2r+\epsilon$: separation needs $(1-v)(2r+\epsilon)>2r$, which fails. So the stated assumption (only diam$/c$) does not ensure non-overlapping supports; the paper claims it does and offers no derivation.

failure_location.quote: The second assumption ensures that wave signals generated at different instants remain separable due to non-overlapping supports.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the second assumption to $c(t_j-t_{j-1})-|a(t_j)-a(t_{j-1})|>\mathrm{diam}\,D_{j-1}$ (or an equivalent direction-dependent condition) and prove the non-overlap of the retarded-time supports.
issues.overall_effect: The reduction of (ISP') to independent single-pulse problems, and hence the proof of Corollary cor:added-1 (which asserts separability under Assumption sump), is unsupported for sources moving toward the receivers at speeds not small compared to $c$.
issues.title: Assumption on pulse spacing does not guarantee separability of signals from a moving source
issues.why_classification: A corrected, slightly stronger hypothesis restores the claim without changing the method, but the stated hypothesis is genuinely insufficient and a short argument must be supplied; the admissible regime narrows somewhat.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the operator $T_{\#}=|\real T| +|\ima T|: X\rightarrow X$ is coercive
We weaken the positivity condition of \cite{GS17,GGH2022} by allowing the source function to vanish on a set of zero measure.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem A.1 requires $T_\#$ coercive, which fails when $S$ has zeros, so the identity for $F$ itself cannot be invoked and the proof instead passes to $\epsilon$-truncated operators. The passage to the limit uses an undefined notion $\lim_{\epsilon\to0}\mathrm{Range}(\cdot)$. Norm convergence $\mathcal F_{\epsilon,\#}^{1/2}\to F_\#^{1/2}$ does not imply any convergence of (non-closed) ranges, and the argument given for $L$ only shows every $g\in\mathrm{Range}(L)$ is a norm limit of $g_\epsilon\in\mathrm{Range}(\mathcal L_\epsilon)$, i.e. it controls closures only. Since all the ranges involved are dense in $L^2(0,K)$, closure-level statements are vacuous and cannot yield equality of the exact ranges. The non-coercive case is exactly where Range$(F_\#^{1/2})$ can be strictly smaller than Range$(L)$, so the conclusion is unestablished.

failure_location.quote: Combining \eqref{RIeps}, \eqref{RIf} and \eqref{RIl}, we obtain the range identity

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either restore the coercivity hypothesis $|S|\ge c_0>0$ on $\overline D$ (so Theorem A.1 applies directly, withdrawing innovation (iii)) or supply a genuinely new proof of the range identity for non-coercive multiplication operators.
issues.overall_effect: The range identity \eqref{RI}, on which the Picard-series indicator functions and all Section 3–4 results rely, is unproven under the paper's relaxed hypothesis $|S|>0$ a.e.; the advertised innovation (iii) is unsupported.
issues.title: Range identity under a.e. positivity proved via ill-defined 'limits of ranges'
issues.why_classification: The proof technique cannot be fixed locally; the only source-supported resolution excludes the advertised regime of sources with nodal sets, and all subsequent results depend on the identity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then we have $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L_N)$ for all $N\geq 1$. By Lemma \ref{lem4.1} (ii), it holds that $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.
Earlier approaches \cite{GS17,GGH2022} relied on test functions integrated over a small spatial domain.

issues.failure_explanation: For $u\in L^2(D)\subset L^1(D)$, $Lu(\tau)=\int_\R e^{-i\tau s}\mu_u(s)\,ds$ where $\mu_u\in L^1$ is the compactly supported pushforward of $u$ under $y\mapsto c^{-1}\hat x\cdot y-t_0$. Hence $Lu$ extends to an entire function which, by Riemann–Lebesgue, tends to 0 as $|\tau|\to\infty$ on $\R$. If $Lu=e^{-i\tau b}$ on $(0,K)$, analyticity forces equality on $\R$, contradicting $|e^{-i\tau b}|=1$. Thus $\phi^{(\hat x)}_{z,\eta}\notin\mathrm{Range}(L)$ for every $z,\eta$, so the 'if' direction of Theorem lem3.4 is false. The proof's error is Lemma lem4.1(ii): '$\mathrm{Range}(L)=\lim_N\mathrm{Range}(L_N)$' is undefined, and any reasonable reading (e.g. union of the finite-dimensional ranges $X_N$, which contain the exponentials) is false, since $X_N\not\subset\mathrm{Range}(L)$; likewise \eqref{RIfN} asserts an unjustified limit of ranges from norm convergence. The converse direction also mishandles boundary points ($b$ an endpoint of the open interval has no $\epsilon$-neighbourhood disjoint from it).

failure_location.quote: For any $\eta \in \R$, there holds $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$ if and only if $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the pointwise exponential by a test function in Range(L) (e.g. the spatially integrated test functions of the cited earlier approaches, $L$ applied to an indicator of a small ball), reprove the range characterization for that class, and redo the Section 4 indicator/uniqueness theorems accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: All indicator functions built from $\phi^{(\hat x)}_{y,\eta}$ have $I^{(\hat x)}_\eta(y)=+\infty$ for every $y$, so $W_\eta\equiv0$, $I^{(\hat x)}\equiv0$, $h\equiv0$, $I\equiv0$: the dichotomies in Theorems Th:factorization, Th:max, Th:kd, TH:hull are false as stated, and the uniqueness theorems thm:added-1, thm:added-2 and Corollary cor:added-1, proved as consequences, lose their proofs. Innovation (ii) ('validation of pointwise test functions') is not established.
issues.title: Pointwise test function is never in Range(L); Theorem lem3.4 is false and its proof rests on an ill-defined limit of ranges
issues.why_classification: The central theorem is false, not merely unproven; every result in Sections 3–4 depends on it, and the only viable fix abandons the paper's pointwise test-function framework in favour of a different construction with new proofs.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The last equality follows from the choice of $\{y_m\} ^{\infty}_{m=1}$ and the fact that $S\in C(\overline{D})$.

issues.failure_explanation: $D\subset\R^3$ has positive volume $|D|$, but $N$ balls of radius $|D|/N$ have total volume $\tfrac{4}{3}\pi|D|^3/N^2\to0$, so condition (ii) cannot hold for large $N$; no admissible sequence $\{y_m\}$ exists. The claimed convergence $\|F_N-F\|\to0$ (an equal-weight Riemann sum with weights $|D|/N$ at arbitrary points) is justified only by this impossible choice, and the displayed estimate also drops the $\tau$-dependence when bounding the supremum. Consequently \eqref{RIfN} and the discretized factorization used in Lemma lem4.1(ii) rest on an undefined construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace condition (ii) by a genuine quadrature: a partition of $D$ into $N$ cells of diameter $\to0$ with nodes $y_m$ and weights equal to cell volumes (adjusting $F_N$ and $T_N$ accordingly), and prove $F_N\to F$ by uniform continuity of the integrand.
issues.overall_effect: The auxiliary discretization underpinning Lemma lem4.1(ii), \eqref{RIfN} and \eqref{RIN} is not well-defined, so the approximation argument in the proof of Theorem lem3.4 is unsupported independently of the limit-of-ranges fallacy.
issues.title: Discretization points required to satisfy an impossible covering condition; convergence $F_N\to F$ unsupported
issues.why_classification: The defect is repairable by a standard but non-trivial replacement of the quadrature construction and its convergence proof; it does not by itself change any stated conclusion beyond what ISSUE-003 already undermines.
